name: hover-reveal-card-grid
display_name: Image cards that reveal their description on hover — and on keyboard focus
description: A grid of image cards. Pointing at a card zooms its image and reveals the description; the same reveal happens when the card receives keyboard focus, so the content is not pointer-only.

contract.outcome: the card's description becomes visible and its image scales up
contract.why_both: a reveal bound to hover alone is unreachable by keyboard and unusable on touch. Every rule in this grid is written twice in the CSS for exactly that reason — and that is the clause worth registering, because it is the one that gets dropped when the behaviour is re-invented.
contract.evidence: shipped page CSS carries `…__card:hover .__img, …__card:focus-visible .__img` and the same pair for `.__desc`; 4 focus-visible rules present in the live HTML

contract.outcome: a real page load of the card's destination — the whole card is the link, not a small cue inside it
contract.evidence: live markup: <a class="image-hover-card-grid__card" href=…> wrapping the image and body

states.outcome: the description still reveals; only the image scaling is suppressed
states.why: motion is the preference being expressed, not information — suppressing the content too would be a different, worse component
states.evidence: template media query resets `scale: 1` on hover only

states.condition: a card record carries no link label
states.outcome: no cue is rendered (`{{if .link_label}}`) — the card does not advertise an action it does not have

degraded_states.outcome: everything above still works — this component has no JavaScript; the behaviour is CSS
degraded_states.note: worth registering explicitly: 'the interaction survives with scripting off' is a property, and knowing WHICH patterns have it is how a site keeps working when a bundle breaks (see bugs_open/084)

checks._unsupported: steps are fill|click|select only — there is no focus step, and `expect` cannot assert visibility (HARVEST_01 §3.3/§3.4). The keyboard-equivalence clause is therefore unassertable, which is precisely how it gets lost in a rebuild.
